note: Six narrow legal-design decisions supplied by the decision owner on 2026-08-29, answering four Blocker-4 terminalization questions and two Oregon route-design questions. Recorded verbatim. These are legal-design decisions about scope and routing; NONE of them is output-level approval of any artifact, and none opens a commercial status. Decisions 5 and 6 in particular change what routes must exist; they do not approve any packet those routes would deliver.

recordedAuthority: Essential condition: Paragraph (1)(c) applies only when no accusatory instrument was filed.
Acquittals and ordinary dismissals are governed by paragraph (1)(d).
The existing broad route currently described as arrests or charges without conviction under ORS 137.225(1)(c) is legally overbroad.
Retire, narrow, or replace that route.
Create a disposition-bound configuration for: NEVER CHARGED / NO ACCUSATORY INSTRUMENT FILED. Authority: ORS 137.225(1)(c). Packet selection: Option 3.

The configuration must require facts proving: no accusatory instrument was filed; the prosecuting attorney elected not to proceed; the statutory 60-day period has elapsed; exact arrest, citation, or charge identity; correct county and prosecuting office.
It may not accept an acquittal or an ordinary dismissal as an equivalent disposition.

Give this configuration its own: route ID; route contract; packet configuration identity; required-fact contract; specification; specification hash; fixture; final-verification contract; artifact binding; output-review record.
requiredFacts: the prosecuting attorney elected not to proceed
exact arrest, citation, or charge identity

recordedAuthority: SEPARATE PACKET SETS ARE REQUIRED.
Essential condition: Use separate disposition-bound packet configurations.
The same statewide OJD form may serve as the base asset: Option 2 for acquittal or dismissal; Option 3 for never-charged matters.
Create at least these three distinct route/configuration treatments:
A. NEVER CHARGED — Authority: ORS 137.225(1)(c) — Form selection: Option 3.
B. ACQUITTAL — Authority: ORS 137.225(1)(d) — Form selection: Option 2.
C. ORDINARY DISMISSAL — Authority: ORS 137.225(1)(d) — Form selection: Option 2.
The same source PDF may be reused as the base asset, but the three treatments may not resolve to one generic or null packet configuration.

Each must have an independently governed: route identity; disposition predicate; packet configuration identity; required facts; selected form option; specification; specification hash; fixture; verification snapshot; artifact-input hash; artifact review; legal/output approval.

If the repository architecture supports one packet family with multiple governed configurations, that is acceptable only when each configuration has a distinct stable identity and cannot be selected by the wrong disposition.
Otherwise, use separate packet-family records.
